goal: Add a pure flywheel.loop_guard module exposing LoopGuardConfig, LoopGuard, and LoopGuardVerdict that detect repeated-failure (STUCK) and thrash from a fed sequence of ToolInteraction tuples.

references: src/flywheel/invoker.py:50-64 -- ToolInteraction (tool_name, tool_input, result.is_error) is the detector input
tests/test_lifecycle_module_purity.py -- mirror this AST-based purity test exactly for the new module
constraints: LoopGuard.observe(interactions: Sequence[ToolInteraction]) -> LoopGuardVerdict | None is the only method; it is fed each iteration's signals.tool_interactions in arrival order and accumulates state across calls within one attempt.
LoopGuardVerdict is a frozen dataclass with: kind (an enum/literal STUCK | THRASH), a human-readable reason, the offending tool_name, and the input digest.

FR-1 repeated-failure: when the same (tool_name, input-digest) tuple yields is_error == True results repeated_tool_failure_threshold times CONSECUTIVELY (across observe calls), return a STUCK verdict.
FR-2 thrash: when an identical (tool_name, input-digest) tuple recurs >= thrash_repeat_threshold times within the trailing thrash_window tool calls (regardless of is_error), return a THRASH verdict.
FR-6 precedence: within a single observe call, evaluate repeated-failure (STUCK) BEFORE thrash (THRASH); a call that is both failing-and-repeating and thrashing returns STUCK.

LoopGuardConfig holds all knobs, each independently disablable via None/0: repeated_tool_failure_threshold, thrash_repeat_threshold, thrash_window, and hang_timeout_seconds (pure data field consumed later by the harness watchdog, NOT by observe). hang_timeout_seconds defaults to None (disabled). The thrash/repeated-failure thresholds default to conservative on-by-default values (they key on byte-identical digests, so a false positive requires the agent to literally repeat itself).
When a threshold is disabled (None/0), that detector early-returns and never trips.

Compute the input digest WITHOUT json (forbidden by the purity test): use hashlib.sha256 over a deterministic structural encoding of tool_input (e.g. a recursively key-sorted repr) so byte-identical inputs collide and key-order noise does not split them.

PURITY: flywheel.loop_guard must import none of json, pathlib, io, asyncio, time and must never call open(); hashlib is permitted. Add tests/test_loop_guard_module_purity.py mirroring tests/test_lifecycle_module_purity.py but with FORBIDDEN_IMPORTS = {json, pathlib, io, asyncio, time}.

Add tests/test_loop_guard.py covering: 3 consecutive identical failing calls trip STUCK at threshold 3; identical successful call repeated past thrash_repeat_threshold within thrash_window trips THRASH; A,B,A,B alternating failures do NOT trip STUCK (consecutive on same digest); identical tuple spread wider than thrash_window does NOT trip THRASH; empty interactions are a no-op; a both-failing-and-thrashing stream returns STUCK (precedence); each disabled threshold never trips.
Call mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on src/flywheel/loop_guard.py and the two new test files and fix all type errors before verify.
Commit with a Conventional Commits message before emitting intent=verify.
non_goals: No hang watchdog logic -- only the hang_timeout_seconds config field lives here as pure data.
No net-diff or input-novelty thrash sub-problems; only literal (tool, digest) repetition.
No persisted/cross-attempt state -- the guard is per-attempt in-memory.
edge_cases: A tool call with result is None (no matching result block) is not a failure for the repeated-failure counter but still counts toward thrash repetition.
Distinct tools failing alternately (A,B,A,B) breaks the consecutive run -- STUCK must not trip.
Within a single observe call carrying many tool calls (one agent turn), the within-call sequence can itself trip a detector.
